fit_reason: SK hynix designs and makes DRAM and NAND flash and is the leading HBM supplier, so it is an HBM, DRAM and flash maker in one. HBM sits next to every accelerator and is the tightest tier, so its makers gain most directly from inference demand and the supply shortage that supports volumes and prices. Memory is the whole business, and SK hynix is one of the world's largest memory makers and the largest HBM supplier to the leading GPU makers.

Micron makes DRAM, NAND flash and NOR memory, including HBM, for cloud servers and data centers, making it an HBM, DRAM and flash maker. Every accelerator needs HBM beside it and the servers around it need DRAM and flash, and tight supply in every tier supports volumes and prices for the makers. Memory is the whole business, and Micron is one of the three major DRAM and HBM makers and the only US-based one.

Sandisk designs and makes NAND flash, SSDs, embedded memory and flash wafers, making it a flash (NAND) maker. Flash is the cheapest tier per bit, and context moving down the tiers adds demand for it while suppliers have added little NAND capacity, which keeps supply tight. Flash is the whole business, and Sandisk is one of the large NAND makers with its own wafer supply and data center SSD line.

Lam Research makes deposition, etch and cleaning equipment, including through-silicon via etch used to stack HBM and the high-aspect-ratio etch used in 3D NAND, making it an equipment supplier. Adding memory capacity requires this equipment, so it gains from volume as the makers build HBM, DRAM and NAND capacity. Memory is a large and meaningful part of its business alongside logic and foundry, and Lam is among the largest wafer fab equipment makers and the most memory-exposed of them.

Applied Materials makes wafer fabrication equipment and services for chipmakers, making it an equipment supplier. Memory makers adding HBM and DRAM capacity need its deposition, etch and materials engineering tools, so it gains from volume as capacity is built. Memory is a meaningful part of its business alongside logic and foundry, and it is the largest wafer fab equipment maker by sales.

Advantest makes semiconductor test systems, including dedicated testers for memory devices, and test handlers, making it an equipment supplier to memory makers. HBM stacks need more testing at more stages than ordinary DRAM, so test equipment gains from volume as HBM and DRAM capacity is built. Memory test is a meaningful part of a business also driven by SoC and AI processor test, and Advantest is the leading supplier of semiconductor test equipment.

Teradyne makes automated test equipment, including its Magnum platform for flash and DRAM, making it an equipment supplier to memory makers. Testing is needed for every memory die and every HBM stack, so it gains from volume as the makers build capacity. Memory test is a meaningful part of its semiconductor test business, which sits alongside robotics and wireless test, and Teradyne is one of the two main chip test equipment makers.

KLA makes wafer inspection, metrology and process control systems used by chipmakers, including memory makers, making it an equipment supplier. Process control is needed on every new memory line and HBM's stacked structure raises yield sensitivity, so it gains from volume as capacity is built. Memory is a meaningful part of a business weighted toward logic and foundry, and KLA is the leading process control supplier.

ASML makes lithography systems, including EUV and DUV, and metrology tools used to pattern every chip, making it an equipment supplier. DRAM makers are adopting EUV for leading nodes, so as they add HBM and DRAM capacity they buy more lithography, and it gains from that volume. Memory is a meaningful part of a business weighted to foundry and logic, and ASML is the sole supplier of EUV lithography.

FormFactor makes probe cards for testing chips at wafer level, including DRAM and NAND/NOR flash, and probing and metrology systems, making it an equipment supplier to memory makers. DRAM and HBM dies are tested before stacking, so probe card demand rises with memory volume as makers build capacity. Memory probe cards are a meaningful part of its business alongside SoC and processor probe cards, and it is a leading probe card supplier.

Entegris supplies specialty chemicals, materials, filtration and wafer handling products to chipmakers, with memory makers among its main customers, making it a materials supplier. Adding memory capacity consumes these materials, so it gains from volume as HBM, DRAM and NAND capacity is built and run. Memory is a meaningful part of a business serving logic and memory fabs alike, and Entegris is a leading supplier of semiconductor process materials.

Rambus sells DDR5 and DDR4 memory interface chips to module makers and licenses memory interface and controller IP and patents, which makes it borderline as a supplier to DRAM module makers rather than a maker itself. Server DRAM is the main memory tier and context moving down the tiers adds demand for it, so its chip volumes follow DRAM module shipments. Memory interfaces are central to its business, and it is one of the main suppliers of DDR5 server module interface chips.

ACM Research makes single-wafer wet cleaning and electroplating equipment for advanced 2D and 3D chip structures, making it an equipment supplier. Cleaning steps multiply with 3D NAND and advanced DRAM, so it gains from volume as memory makers build capacity. Memory is a meaningful part of its business, which leans on Chinese chipmakers, and it is a smaller player than the large equipment makers.

Kulicke and Soffa makes semiconductor assembly equipment, including thermo-compression and flip-chip bonders and wafer-level bonders, making it an equipment supplier. Thermo-compression bonding is used to stack HBM dies, so it can gain from volume as HBM capacity grows. Memory stacking is a meaningful but smaller part of a business weighted to wire bonding and general assembly, and it is a mid-sized player in advanced packaging equipment.

Camtek makes inspection and metrology systems for advanced packaging and memory components, making it an equipment supplier. HBM stacking and advanced packaging need more inspection, so it gains from volume as memory makers add HBM capacity. Memory and HBM inspection are a meaningful part of its business alongside other packaging applications, and it is a specialist in this niche.

Onto Innovation makes defect inspection, optical metrology and packaging lithography systems for chipmakers and advanced packaging, making it an equipment supplier. Its tools serve HBM and advanced packaging lines, so it gains from volume as memory makers build capacity. Memory is a meaningful part of a business spread across logic, packaging and specialty devices, and it is a mid-sized process control supplier.

Nova makes dimensional, film and materials metrology systems for logic, foundry and memory producers, making it an equipment supplier. Process control is needed on new memory lines, so it gains from volume as the makers add capacity. Memory is a meaningful part of its customer base, and Nova is a focused metrology supplier, smaller than the largest process control makers.

ASM International makes deposition equipment, including atomic layer deposition, epitaxy and furnaces, making it an equipment supplier. ALD layers are used in DRAM and 3D NAND, so it gains from volume as memory makers build capacity. Memory is a meaningful but smaller part of a business weighted to leading-edge logic, and ASM is the leading ALD supplier.

Axcelis makes ion implantation systems for chip fabrication, making it an equipment supplier. Memory makers use implant in DRAM and NAND production, so it gains from volume as they add capacity. Memory is a meaningful part of a business also weighted to power and mature-node chips, and it is a leading implant supplier in a small niche.

MKS makes vacuum, gas and power delivery subsystems for etch and deposition tools, plus lasers and photonics, making it a supplier of equipment components. Its subsystems go into the etch and deposition tools memory makers buy to add capacity, so it gains from volume. Semiconductor equipment is a meaningful part of a business also serving PCB, industrial and life sciences markets, and it is a mid-sized subsystem supplier.

Ultra Clean supplies gas and chemical delivery subsystems, process modules and chamber cleaning services to semiconductor equipment makers, making it a supplier of equipment components. As memory makers build capacity they buy more tools that contain these subsystems, so it gains from volume. Semiconductor equipment is central to its business but memory is one end market among several, and it is a mid-sized subsystem supplier.

Ichor makes gas and chemical delivery subsystems for semiconductor etch, deposition and cleaning tools, making it a supplier of equipment components. Memory capacity additions drive orders for those tools and their subsystems, so it gains from volume. Semiconductor equipment is its whole business but memory is one end market, and it is a smaller subsystem supplier dependent on a few equipment makers.

Qnity supplies electronic materials and solutions used to manufacture semiconductor chips, making it a materials supplier. Adding and running memory capacity consumes process materials, so it gains from volume as memory makers expand. The description is thin on how much of its business is memory, and it is a newly separated materials business.

Photronics makes photomasks used to pattern integrated circuits, with operations in Korea and Taiwan where memory fabs are concentrated, making it a materials supplier. New memory designs and capacity need new masks, so it gains from volume as memory makers expand. Memory is a meaningful but unquantified part of a business also serving logic and flat panel displays, and it is a mid-sized merchant mask maker.

Veeco makes laser annealing, ion beam, deposition, wet processing and packaging lithography equipment used in making logic and DRAM, making it an equipment supplier. DRAM makers use its annealing and process tools as they add capacity, so it gains from volume. DRAM is a meaningful part of a business also serving photonics, power and hard disk heads, and it is a smaller equipment supplier.

Cohu makes automated test equipment, test handlers and interface components for chipmakers and test houses, making it a test equipment supplier. Memory test volumes rise as makers build capacity, which can add handler and interface demand. Memory is a modest part of a business weighted to automotive, industrial and mobile chips, and it is a smaller test supplier.

Silicon Motion designs NAND flash controllers for client and enterprise SSDs and embedded storage, selling to NAND makers and hyperscalers, which makes it borderline as a supplier to flash makers rather than a maker itself. Flash demand grows as context moves down the tiers, and controller volumes follow SSD shipments. Flash is central to its business, and it is the leading merchant NAND controller supplier.

Penguin Solutions makes DRAM modules, SSDs and flash storage in its Integrated Memory segment alongside HPC and AI computing systems, which makes it borderline as a module maker rather than a chip maker. Server DRAM and flash demand rises with AI deployments and tight supply supports pricing through the chain. Memory is a meaningful segment of a business also spanning advanced computing and LEDs, and it is a small specialty module supplier.

Western Digital is described as making HDDs, flash-based SSDs and flash memory wafers, which would make it a flash maker, but it has since spun off its flash business as Sandisk and now mainly makes hard drives, so its fit is borderline. Flash demand grows as context moves down the tiers, but hard drives sit below the flash tier described for memory. The flash share of its business is now small or none, though it remains a leading data center hard drive maker.

Seagate makes mass-capacity nearline hard drives and some SSDs, which makes it borderline since hard drives sit below the memory tiers. Its SSDs give it limited exposure to flash demand as context moves down the tiers. Flash is a small part of a business dominated by hard drives, where Seagate is a leading supplier.

Everpure, formerly Pure Storage, sells data storage solutions built on flash, which makes it borderline as a buyer and integrator of flash rather than a flash maker. Context moving down the tiers adds demand for flash storage in AI data centers, which can lift its volumes. Flash storage is central to its business, and it is a leading all-flash enterprise storage vendor, though the description is thin.

NetApp sells data management software and storage systems including All-Flash FAS arrays, which makes it borderline as a flash storage integrator rather than a maker. Flash demand from AI data centers can add to its all-flash array sales. Flash hardware is a meaningful part of a business heavy in software and cloud data services, and it is a major enterprise storage vendor.

Astera Labs makes data, network and memory connectivity chips for cloud and AI infrastructure, including memory connectivity, which makes it borderline as a supplier around the memory tiers rather than a maker. Products that extend and pool memory help add capacity behind accelerators as context grows, which the memory section describes as more memory tiers. Memory connectivity is a meaningful but smaller part of a business led by PCIe and network connectivity, and it is a fast-growing specialist.

Marvell makes SSD and HDD storage controllers, CXL switches and NVMe interfaces alongside custom ASICs and networking chips, which makes it borderline as a supplier around the memory tiers. CXL memory expansion and SSD demand add capacity behind accelerators as context moves down the tiers. Memory and storage are a modest part of a business led by data center networking and custom silicon, though Marvell is a major data center chip supplier.

Netlist makes memory subsystems such as DIMMs, NVDIMMs and DRAM-plus-NAND hybrid modules for servers and resells DRAM, NAND and SSDs, which makes it borderline as a module maker rather than a chip maker. Server DRAM and flash are tight tiers, so module and resale volumes can benefit from demand. Memory is central to its business, but it is a small player whose value rests heavily on its memory patents.

Aehr makes wafer-level and packaged-part burn-in and test systems for logic, optical and memory devices, making it a test equipment supplier. Memory test and burn-in could add orders as makers build capacity. Memory is a small part of a business weighted to silicon carbide and AI processor burn-in, and it is a small niche supplier.

Solstice Advanced Materials supplies specialty materials, including for semiconductor manufacturing processes, making it a materials supplier. Semiconductor materials demand rises as memory makers add capacity. Semiconductor materials are one part of a business also spanning refrigerants, cooling, fibers and packaging, so memory is a small share, and the description is thin on its position.
